merger_description:
CAMP Australia Pty Ltd, which is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of CA Group Holdco Pty Ltd (together, **Camp Australia**), proposes to acquire 20 outside school hours care (**OSHC**) businesses and their associated assets from Jabiru Community Services Limited (**Jabiru**) by way of asset sale (the Acquisition).

Camp Australia is a Victoria-headquartered, national OSHC services provider, delivering before school care, after school care, pupil free day care and vacation care programmes to primary school-aged children in all states and territories. Camp Australia provides services at approximately 442 schools across Australia, including 68 services in Queensland. Camp Australia is owned by a consortium of private investment funds led by Allegro Funds.

Jabiru is a not-for-profit organisation headquartered in Bracken Ridge Queensland and provides OSHC programmes to primary-school aged children in South-East Queensland. Jabiru currently provides OSHC services at 22 schools in Queensland, 20 of which are the subject of the Acquisition.

Camp Australia and Jabiru overlap in the supply of OSHC services and vacation care services in Queensland.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, requests for information, information from third
partes, and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• Camp Australia would continue to face competition from
multiple alternative suppliers of OSHC services and vacation
care services in south-east Queensland.
• Some third-party feedback raised concerns that the Acquisition
could decrease service quality, reduce diversity of providers
(given the removal of Jabiru as a not-for-profit supplier), and
increase barriers for smaller suppliers. However, given the
presence of remaining alternative suppliers, and taking into
account other information, including the role of the Queensland
Department of Education in managing arrangements for the
supply of OSHC services, the ACCC considers that the
Acquisition is unlikely to decrease service quality, diversity of
providers or increase barriers for smaller suppliers as a result of
a substantial lessening of competition for the supply of OSHC
and vacation care services in south-east Queensland.
